1.title: Identify Patterns and Trends
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Identify Patterns and Trends. It covers the exam area Visualize and analyze the data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Use the Analyze feature in Power B I. Use grouping, binning, and clustering. Use A I visuals. Use reference lines, error bars, and forecasting. Detect outliers and anomalies. Use Copilot to summarize the underlying semantic model. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Visualize and analyze the data (twenty-five-thirty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: AI visuals: which one answers which question
1.text: A I visuals: which one answers which question. Power B I has four A I visuals, and each one answers a different kind of question. The exam tests the match.

1.title: AI visuals: which one answers which question, continued
1.text: A I visuals: which one answers which question. The figure shows this: Four A I visuals matched to the question each answers: key influencers, decomposition tree, smart narrative and Q and A.

1.title: AI visuals: which one answers which question, continued
1.text: A I visuals: which one answers which question. Key influencers. Question it answers: What drives a metric to be high, low or a given category? Key settings: Analyze, Explain by, Expand by; tabs Key influencers and Top segments. Decomposition tree. Question it answers: How does one measure break down across dimensions, in any order? Key settings: Analyze is the measure; Explain by holds the dimensions; A I splits choose High value or Low value.

1.title: AI visuals: which one answers which question, continued
1.text: A I visuals: which one answers which question. Smart narrative. Question it answers: Can I read the story of a visual or page as text? Key settings: Text with dynamic values that follow the filters. Q and A visual. Question it answers: Can users ask a question in plain language? Key settings: A question box and suggested questions.

1.title: AI visuals: which one answers which question, continued
1.text: A I visuals: which one answers which question. Key influencers supports categorical or continuous analysis and does not support Direct Query. In a decomposition tree you can lock a level, so the A I does not change it. Smart narrative is the older mode. The narrative visual with Copilot (Module ten) is the newer one. Q and A experiences are going away in February twenty twenty-seven. Microsoft recommends Copilot instead. Exam tip: Key influencers explains why a metric is high or low; the decomposition tree breaks one measure down and lets you drill into the biggest part. If the question says "drivers" or "what affects", choose key influencers. Exam tip: Q and A experiences are going away in February twenty twenty-seven, and Microsoft recommends Copilot. Expect Copilot as the modern answer for natural language questions.

1.title: Analyze, grouping, binning and clustering
1.text: Analyze, grouping, binning and clustering. Analyze explains a change with one right-click. Right-click a data point on a bar or line chart, choose Analyze, then pick one option. Explain the increase. Finds the factors behind a rise at that point. Explain the decrease. Finds the factors behind a fall at that point. Find where this distribution is different. Finds what makes that distribution unlike the others. The default output is a waterfall chart. Analyze is not supported on Direct Query, on a live connection or on a model with row-level security. The first data point has no insight. Grouping, binning and clustering create categories for a visual.

1.title: Analyze, grouping, binning and clustering, continued
1.text: Analyze, grouping, binning and clustering. Grouping. How you make it: Ctrl plus select data points, then Group. Result: A field named "(groups)"; edit the groups; an Other group holds the rest. Binning. How you make it: Choose a numeric or time field, then set the Bin size. Result: A field named "(bins)"; not available for measures. Clustering. How you make it: Use a scatter chart. Result: Automatically groups similar points; you can choose the number of clusters. Exam tip: Grouping is hand-picked, binning is equal-size ranges, clustering is automatic on a scatter chart. Bins work on numeric and time fields, never on measures.

1.title: Reference lines, error bars and forecasting
1.text: Reference lines, error bars and forecasting. All of these live in the Analytics pane of a selected visual. Which visual supports which item is a favorite question. Constant line. Where it works: X or Y axis. Notes: A fixed value you type, such as a target. Min, max, average, median, percentile lines. Where it works: Visuals with the pane. Notes: Calculated from the data; percentile lines are for imported data. Trend line. Where it works: Line, area and column charts. Notes: Shows the direction of the data. Forecast. Where it works: Line chart only. Notes: Set the forecast length and the confidence interval.

1.title: Reference lines, error bars and forecasting, continued
1.text: Reference lines, error bars and forecasting. Symmetry shading. Where it works: Scatter chart only. Notes: Shades the plot to show where one axis is higher than the other. Error bars. Where it works: Bar, column and line charts. Notes: Show a range of uncertainty around each value. Anomalies. Where it works: Line chart only. Notes: See section four. Exam tip: Forecast works only on a line chart. A trend line works on line, area and column charts; error bars on bar, column and line charts.

1.title: Outliers, anomalies and Copilot summaries
1.text: Outliers, anomalies and Copilot summaries. Outliers are values far from the rest. Show them on a scatter chart, where outliers sit away from the main group. Add average, median or percentile lines to judge the distance. Anomaly detection finds unusual points in a time series. Turn it on in the Analytics pane.

1.title: Outliers, anomalies and Copilot summaries, continued
1.text: Outliers, anomalies and Copilot summaries. Visual. A line chart with a time series axis. Data. At least four data points. Settings. A sensitivity setting; Explain by gives possible explanations. Does not work with. A legend, multiple or secondary values, or a forecast or reference lines on the same chart. To summarize the semantic model, ask Copilot to summarize it. Copilot can also add descriptions to measures. The requirements are the same as in Module ten. A paid Fabric capacity F two or higher, or Premium P one or higher. A trial, or Pro or P P U alone, is not enough.

2.title: Outliers, anomalies and Copilot summaries, continued
2.text: Outliers, anomalies and Copilot summaries. The Copilot tenant setting turned on, and a supported region. After you buy capacity, Copilot can take up to twenty-four hours to appear. Row-level and object-level security still apply to what Copilot can see. Exam tip: Anomaly detection fails when the chart has a legend, a secondary value, a forecast or a reference line. Remove them first. Exam tip: Copilot needs a paid Fabric capacity F two or higher, or Premium P one or higher. Pro or P P U alone does not turn it on.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A retailer's line chart shows monthly sales, and March is much higher than February. An analyst wants to see which factors explain the rise. What should the analyst do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Right-click the March point and choose Analyze, then Explain the increase. Analyze with Explain the increase finds the factors behind a rise at one data point; trend lines, forecasts and bins do not explain a change.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A finance team wants to learn which customer attributes are most associated with a low satisfaction rating. Which visual should it add? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A key influencers visual with the rating in Analyze. Key influencers ranks the fields that drive a metric; a decomposition tree only breaks a measure down.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A finance team wants to extend monthly revenue three months ahead, with a confidence interval. Which visual type must it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A line chart showing revenue by month. The forecast option is available on line charts only.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A line chart with a date axis shows daily orders for three regions in a legend. An analyst turns on anomaly detection and gets no results. What should the analyst do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Remove the legend so the chart has one series. Anomaly detection does not work with a legend, so one series on a time axis is needed; a forecast or a constant line would also block it.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. An analyst has a numeric Age column and needs a column chart of customers by ten-year ranges. What should the analyst create? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A bin on the Age column with a bin size of ten. Binning cuts a numeric field into equal-size ranges, and it cannot be applied to a measure.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A team has Pro licenses and a trial capacity. A developer wants Copilot to summarize a semantic model and add measure descriptions, but Copilot is unavailable. What does the team need? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A paid Fabric capacity F two or higher. Copilot needs a paid Fabric capacity F two or higher, or Premium P one or higher; a trial, Pro or P P U alone is not enough.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which pane holds the forecast, trend line and error bars? Answer: The Analytics pane. Question two. Which chart type is the only one that supports a forecast? Answer: The line chart. Question three. Name three situations where Analyze is not supported. Answer: Direct Query, a live connection and a model with row-level security.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is happening to Q and A experiences in February twenty twenty-seven? Answer: They are going away, and Microsoft recommends Copilot. Question five. Which kind of field cannot be binned? Answer: A measure. Question six. On which chart type does clustering work? Answer: A scatter chart.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Analyze: right-click a point on a bar or line chart. Key influencers: Analyze, Explain by, Expand by; not Direct Query; answers "what drives it". Decomposition tree: measure in Analyze, dimensions in Explain by; High value or Low value splits. Smart narrative, Q and A: text summary with dynamic values. Grouping, binning, clustering: group by Ctrl plus select; bins for numeric and time fields, not measures. Analytics pane: forecast on line charts only; trend line on line, area and column. Anomalies: line chart with a time axis, at least four points. Copilot summary: summarize the model, add measure descriptions; paid F two or higher, or P one or higher.
